newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WALSH, LLOYD PREDICT LARA FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WALSH, LLOYD PREDICT LARA FIGHTBACK.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh said on Tuesday he was confident star batsman Brian Lara would turn his poor form around in the same way his side had fought back to beat Australia in the third test.

Lara, who holds the world records for the highest scores in test and first-class cricket, has endured a dismal run of form during West Indies' tour of Australia, making a total of only 77 runs in his six test innings on tour.
While Lara failed again in the third test in Melbourne last week, West Indies fought back to stun Australia by winning in three days.
Walsh told reporters in Brisbane he though Lara would soon emulate the example set by the rest of the team in Melbourne.
"It's coming for him. It's not too far around the corner," Walsh said.
Walsh's opinion was echoed by former captain and tour manager Clive Lloyd, who believed the measure of greatness was the way players fought their way out of trouble.
"He's such a great player," Lloyd said. "It's just how you pick yourself up, so he's got to assess the situation."

West Indies had suffered an embarrassing losing streak of seven matches before the Melbourne test. Lloyd said that win had saved the tour, with West Indies keeping the five-test series alive as they also attempt to fight back in the World Series Cup limited overs competition.
"We picked ourselves up off the floor and won the third test," Lloyd said.
"We realised if we didn't do well in Melbourne the tour would have collapsed... it would have been quite flat.
"(Melbourne) was one of the best test matches we have ever played. We've been a good side that has been playing badly, but we have turned the corner," he said.
Lloyd's only concern was that his side would now have to play a string of World Series limited overs match before the fourth test, starting in Adelaide on January 25.
"Sometimes there is too much chopping and changing," Lloyd said. "We are going to have to look at that in the future."
West Indies' next match is against Pakistan in the three-team World Series Cup in Brisbane on Friday.
